text:
Maya Patel: quick question — for canary rollouts do we want region-first failover or model-variant-first as the default automatic fallback? thinking about user-perceived correctness vs cost.
Alex Gomez: +1 to discussing. region-first keeps model choice constant, so fewer regressions. but cross-region latency could spike. :thinking:
Sasha Ivanov: model-variant-first reduces cross-region hops, cheaper if smaller quantized variants exist. but riskier for quality regressions. we should guard by eval delta and prompt-level regressions.
Zane Li: implementation note: routing-service can short-circuit by policy key. we already support a weight-based plan and a quick 'fallback_chain' array on routes. can extend to order by [region, variant, fallback_pool].
Liz Chen: product question — what control do we expose in Console? do we let customers pick order or offer curated presets like "latency-optimized", "quality-first", "balanced"?
Maya Patel: I like presets. default should be safe for most apps. maybe "balanced" = try local region -> variant fallback -> multi-region.
Jen Ortega: ops: also need to consider quota accounting. if we failover to a cheaper variant but cross over into another billing boundary, customers get surprised. console should show estimated cost delta in rollout preview.
Alex Gomez: agree. also need telemetry triggers for auto-fallback: e.g., p95 latency > 350ms for 30s AND error-rate > 1% -> trigger capacity fallback. thresholds need per-route overrides.
Sasha Ivanov: propose these signals for the decision engine: [p95_latency, request_error_rate, model_confidence_drop, kv_cache_miss_rate, active_inflight_concurrency]. fallback only if two of the five exceed thresholds for a sliding window.
Maya Patel: sounds good. can we express that as a small DSL so Console can render/edit it?
Zane Li: example policy sketch — plz bikeshed names: ```yaml
fallback_policy:
  preset: balanced
  order: [region, variant, capacity_pool]
  triggers:
    - name: latency_surge
      condition: p95_latency > 350ms
      duration: 30s
    - name: error_surge
      condition: error_rate > 1%
      duration: 60s
  arbitration:
    require: 2_of_3
```
Liz Chen: nice. UI bits: preview should show which variant/region would be used for a sample request set, plus cost delta and expected latency change. add a "dry-run" mode that logs but doesn't reroute.
Jen Ortega: also we need rate-limiter hooks so fallback doesn't amplify load on secondary pools. throttling should be part of the policy: ramp to X% over Y seconds.
Sasha Ivanov: good call. add "ramp_up" param. also add a backoff if secondary latency worsens.
Alex Gomez: operational concern: when a canary hits quality regression we should prefer model-variant rollback instead of region failover. order matters per-failure-type. maybe policies can map failure_type -> order.
Maya Patel: yes — separate "failure_types" mapping. e.g., quality_regression -> [variant, rollback]; infra_degradation -> [region, capacity_pool].
Zane Li: routing-service change: store policy as JSON on route, evaluation engine evaluates triggers and returns an ordered list of candidate endpoints. short-circuit rules: if model_confidence_drop > X then immediate variant rollback.
infra-bot: deploybot: Canary deployment 2024-06-xxT12:45:10Z started for route /v1/generate (canary id=canary-827)
Maya Patel: @infra-bot noted. good time to prototype the policy in staging.
Liz Chen: sprint ask: can we get Console mock of presets + preview by end of sprint? I'll slot it as P1 for rollout UX.
Zane Li: engineering: I'll add the policy schema and a simple decision engine in the routing-service. estimate 4 dev-days + 2 for integration tests.
Sasha Ivanov: I'll produce a minimal eval set to detect quality regressions automatically and wire it to telemetry.
Jen Ortega: ops: we'll add quota/billing flags and safety rate-limiter hooks. need a changelog entry for customers about default behaviour.
Alex Gomez: small API debate: should policy be part of public Route API or enterprise-only feature? leaning public but with conservative defaults.
Maya Patel: leaning public too. defaults keep you safe; enterprise plans can tweak aggressive options like cross-region fallback.
Liz Chen: design note: rename "fallback" -> "safety leash" in UI to reduce scary language? open to bikeshedding. :smile:
Sasha Ivanov: final nit: need clear metrics exposed in Console for when an automatic fallback happened (reason + decision path). otherwise debugging is painful.
Maya Patel: agreed. add a breadcrumb on request traces: fallback.executed = {reason, chosen_endpoint, before_metrics, after_metrics}.
Zane Li: will add structured logs and a lightweight trace span.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone — next steps: Zane start schema PR, Sasha eval harness, Jen ensure quota hooks, Liz mock UI. we'll sync mid-week. :thumbsup:
